mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an easing monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when FEDFUNDS declines, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS trend and SPX returns is less than 0.1 in absolute value over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of months when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or the average return in triggered months is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals a sectoral shift toward construction-driven economic activity that boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (INDPRO decline and HOUST rise) fails to predict positive returns in more than 50% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression of SPX returns on INDPRO and HOUST is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation periods (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% year-over-year), a federal funds rate increase above 4.5% triggers monetary tightening that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past three months indicates robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO trend fails to predict positive returns in more than 50% of months, or the correlation between INDPRO growth and SPX returns is less than 0.15 in absolute value over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1,700,000 units in a month, it signals a contraction in residential construction that reduces consumer wealth and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of months when HOUST < 1700, or the average return in such months is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and rise in real personal consumption (RSAFS) signals strong labor market conditions and expanding consumer spending that drives corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (UNRATE decline and RSAFS rise) fails to predict positive returns in more than 50% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression of SPX returns on UNRATE and RSAFS is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions (GDP growth > 2.5% annualized), a decline in real personal consumption (RSAFS) signals an impending slowdown that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions (GDPC1 growth > 2.5% annualized), SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of months when RSAFS declines, or the average return in such months is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).
